record.paper_title: Some open questions concerning biological growth
record.context_brief: Role of Galilean invariance in KPZ scaling exponents
record.original_question: If the dilution KPZ equation on a growing domain obeys traditional KPZ scaling in some suitable limit even though Galilean invariance is lost, what does that imply about the role of Galilean invariance in fixing the KPZ critical exponents and the scaling relation α + z = 2?

evidence.quote: If it were found that the dilution equat ion (33) obeys the traditional KPZ scaling (at least in some suitable limit), then that would put into question the role that Galilean invariance has in ﬁxing the exponents. The KPZ c ritical exponents are believed to obey the scaling relation α + z = 2 in all spatial dimensions, a relation that has been traditionally attributed to Galilean invariance, although this interpretation has been recently put into question [25, 26, 27, 28].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Kardar–Parisi–Zhang (KPZ) equation for an interface height field h(x,t) on a d-dimensional substrate,
  ∂_t h = ν Δh + (λ/2)|∇h|^2 + η(x,t),
where η is Gaussian white noise. Its stationary scaling is characterized by a roughness exponent α and a dynamic exponent z, satisfying h(bx, b^z t) ≃ b^α h(x,t) in distribution. The exact relation
  α + z = 2
is conventionally derived from the invariance of the KPZ equation under the infinitesimal Galilean (tilt) transformation h(x,t) → h(x + λv t, t) + v·x, which forces λ to be unrenormalized.

Now consider a "dilution" variant of the KPZ equation that models a growing domain, in which the nonlinear and noise terms are dressed by a time-dependent dilution factor associated with domain growth. This modification breaks the standard Galilean (tilt) invariance.

Question: Suppose one establishes (in some appropriate scaling limit) that this dilution KPZ equation exhibits the same critical exponents α and z as the standard KPZ universality class, in particular the scaling relation α + z = 2. What does such a result imply about the necessity of Galilean invariance for fixing the KPZ critical exponents and for the scaling relation α + z = 2? Specifically, can α + z = 2 be derived from a principle independent of Galilean invariance, and if so, identify the symmetry, Ward identity, or non-perturbative mechanism that enforces it.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has argued, via dynamic renormalization-group analyses of non-Galilean-invariant KPZ-like models (including discretized and dilution-type variants), that the relation α+z=2 can emerge from exact cancellations in vertex renormalization without requiring Galilean invariance. This supports the interpretation that Galilean invariance is sufficient but not necessary for the KPZ scaling relation. A complete, rigorous identification of the underlying mechanism in all dimensions remains incomplete, so the broader question is best regarded as partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the role of Galilean invariance in KPZ
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of whether Galilean invariance is essential for KPZ exponents.
status_evidence.claim: The role of Galilean invariance in fixing KPZ exponents has been re-examined.

status_evidence.title: KPZ equation: Galilean-invariance violation, consistency, and fluctuation-dissipation issues in real-space discretization
status_evidence.snippet: Real-space discretizations of KPZ violate Galilean invariance yet can still display KPZ scaling.
status_evidence.claim: Models violating Galilean invariance can still exhibit α+z=2.

status_evidence.title: KPZ. Recent developments via a variational formulation
status_evidence.snippet: Review of KPZ developments including discussions of symmetries and exponents.
status_evidence.claim: Galilean invariance is one route to α+z=2 but the relation has been derived from variational/other methods.
